actionItems.action: Add a Privacy Notice (also called a Privacy Policy) to your app. It must explain what personal data you collect, why you collect it, how long you keep it, and who can access it. This is required by GDPR Article 13.
Document these data flows in your Records of Processing Activities. Every organisation that handles personal data must keep a written record of what they process and why (GDPR Article 30).
Make sure stored personal data can be deleted when a user asks (the 'Right to Erasure' under GDPR Article 17). Add a way for users to request deletion of their account or data.

This app captures photos, audio or video. If these show or record identifiable people, that is likely biometric / special-category data (GDPR Article 9) and, for under-18s, children's data (Article 8). You need an Article 9 condition, a DPIA, clear consent/notice, strict retention limits, and access controls. Confirm exactly what is captured and stored.

File uploads need extra care. Before uploading, tell users what you do with their files, how long you keep them, and who can see them. If uploads might contain photos of people, this could require a DPIA.

Your app integrates third-party / cloud services (Supabase). For each one, confirm whether personal data is sent to it, put a Data Processing Agreement in place with the supplier, and check where it stores and processes data. A location outside the UK/EEA needs a documented international-transfer safeguard (GDPR Articles 44–49).

Confirm the hosting region / data residency for each external service listed above. This is usually not visible in the code — ask the supplier (or check their dashboard) whether personal data stays in the UK/EEA. This feeds the DPIA (international transfers) and the IT System Requirements Assessment.
